### Summary

This section describes main at snapy@9ad0936779ae001dba65c9eafccaa7c058686c97, after chengcli/snapy#303, while the rest of the book is
pinned at snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Default: **on**. This switch defaults on, including an empty string; it is read once per process in
`gravity_work_radial_exact` ([`hydro.cpp:256-266`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/9ad0936779ae001dba65c9eafccaa7c058686c97/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L256-L266)). It acts only with nonzero radial gravity,
`gravity-work: face` (the default since chengcli/snapy#303, `gravity_work` [`const_gravity.cpp:28`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/9ad0936779ae001dba65c9eafccaa7c058686c97/src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp#L28)) and a grid with an
$x_1$ measure: Cartesian, spherical-polar or gnomonic-equiangle (cubed sphere). A grid without one (cylindrical)
warns once and retains ordinary face work; a periodic $x_1$ column warns once as well.
Use the corrected potential energy in @eq-ch12-radial-exact-budget for its budget, not the plain centroid sum.
The internal alias is option F (corrected-PE work).
:::

### Derivation

For constant $g_1$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, $\phi=-g_1x_1$ in $\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}}$.
Integrating the product of locally linear density and potential gives
$\langle\rho\phi\rangle_{V_i}=\rho_i\phi_i-g_1\sigma_i^2\partial_1\rho$.
Replace the derivative by the centroid quadratic slope $s_i[\rho]$ to define $P$.
On gnomonic-equiangle grids $P$ gains $-g_1(r_c-x_{1v})\rho_i$ per unit volume and the work the matching
$g_1(r_c-x_{1v})\Delta\rho_i$ (@sec-ch06-dwork). On a fixed mesh this is a linear functional of density, so its time difference uses exactly the same slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
P&=\sum_iV_i\left(\rho_i\phi_i-g_1\sigma_i^2s_i[\rho]\right),\\
\Delta P&=\sum_iV_i\left(\phi_i\Delta\rho_i-g_1\sigma_i^2s_i[\Delta\rho]\right).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch12-radial-exact-budget}

Ordinary face work cancels the first term (with the boundary potential-energy flux). Adding
$g_1\sigma_i^2s_i[\Delta\rho]$ to the energy increment cancels the second term, cell by cell.
`corrected_pe_work` implements that increment ([`gravity_work_radial.hpp:94-128`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/9ad0936779ae001dba65c9eafccaa7c058686c97/src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp#L94-L128)).
For implicit work the density increment must be the actual post-clamp increment. The conserved discrete budget is exact
up to arithmetic and boundary fluxes; its approximation of smooth continuous potential energy has truncation error.
`configuration_check.py` verifies the cancellation for a fixed linear slope matrix.
Source derivation: `docs/derivations/curved-gravity-work-weight.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §7.

### Numerical method

The slope is quadratic through three `x1v` nodes, one-sided only at physical walls: at an internal $x_1$ seam the
explicit work exchanges one row of the stage's density change and takes the centred slope, and the logged `pe=`
reads the exchanged ghost density. A periodic $x_1$ column keeps the one-sided slope at its seams. An implicit
scheme refuses any $x_1$ split. On gnomonic-equiangle grids, where `x1v` is the face midpoint, the work also books
$g_1(r_c-x_{1v})\Delta\rho$ (@sec-ch06-dwork).
Use the cell measure variance, not the lateral face variance. Explicit face work and the implicit operator use the
same corrected budget; active solids mask energy deposition. On unsupported grids the setup warning does not abort.
The switch is inactive for `face-wallc`, whose wall cells keep cell work. Corrected work replaces the cp3/cp5/weno5 curvature work instead of adding to it, avoiding a double correction.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The gnomonic grid receives corrected work since chengcli/snapy#303; a lone gnomonic block with reflecting lateral
walls loses mass under lateral flow, switch on or off (chengcli/snapy#301). Split and unsplit $x_1$ columns agree,
except on a periodic $x_1$ column, whose seams keep the one-sided slope.

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::
